miQCadj

miQCadj provides extensions and utilities for miQC quality-control cell filtering in Seurat and SummarizedExperiment workflows.

The original miQC package uses a two-component mixture model fitted with flexmix to model mitochondrial transcript percentage as a function of cellular complexity and identify potentially low-quality cells in single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets.

miQCadj extends this workflow with additional model specifications, configurable component selection, posterior-probability-based classification, and post-hoc geometric validation. It provides both an implementation of the original miQC classification adjustments and an alternative geometry-based approach, allowing users to inspect and compare adjusted cell classifications before transferring the selected results back to their input objects.

Installation

You can install miQCadj from GitHub using

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ghostlab-id/miQCadj")

Alternatively, devtools can be used for installation.

Exported Functions

Exported functions comprise (alphabetically ordered):

Function Purpose
add_to_input_obj() Add results to the Input object
adjust_classification() Post-hoc Adjustments of cell classifications
check_miQC_components() Visualize fitted miQC components and posterior classifications
check_miQC_predictions() Visualize cell classifications after geometry validation
define_classification() Define components and posterior cutoff for cell classification
geometry_adjustments() Adjusted geometric validation of selected miQC classifications
original_adjustments() Original geometric validation of selected miQC classifications
run_miQCadj() Fit a two-component mixture model

Basic workflow

Load package and fit a flexmix mixture model:

library(miQCadj)
flexmix_list <- run_miQCadj(sc_data)

By default a linear model (model_type = “linear”) facilitating intercept-based component selection will be used.

Visualize component identities and posterior probabilities of cells belonging to the low-quality component:

plots <- check_miQC_components(flexmix_list)

By default the ggplot objects are combined into a 1x2 plot grid. To return a list of ggplot objects set combine_plots = FALSE.

Define component selection mode and posterior probability threshold filtering:

flexmix_list <- define_classification(flexmix_list)

By default the component selection using intercepts (component_selection = "intercept") and a posterior probability threshold of posterior_cutoff=0.75 will be used.

Adjust predictions using geometric plausibility checks:

flexmix_list <- adjust_classification(flexmix_list)

By default post-hoc adjustments as implemented in the original miQC package as well as adjusted geometric adjustments are performed (adjustment_method = c("original_check", "geometry_check")). Both adjustment methods can be used independently, but should be added by adjust_classification(), if requested in downstream analysis.

Inspect adjusted predictions:

plots <- check_miQC_predictions(flexmix_list)

By default plots for both post-hoc adjustment methods (adjustment_method = c("original_check", "geometry_check")) are created and combined into a 2x2 patchwork grid. The unmodified prediction plots can be added, setting add_unadjusted_prediction = TRUE.

Select final predictions and add data back to the input object:

sc_data <- add_to_input_obj(flexmix_list = flexmix_list, 
                            input_obj = sc_data, 
                            adjustment_method="geometry_check")

The final prediction based on the selected flexmix model, component mode, posterior cutoff, and adjustment method will be available in the input object meta data columns, enabling further validation or filtering.

By default the related information will also be saved to the input object, and will be available in the misc slot for Seurat objects or in the metadata slot for SummarizedExperiment objects.

Vignettes

For further information please check the package vignette: miQC_pbmcsca

Notes

miQCadj is designed for exploratory and reproducible QC workflows. Though, the predictions made by miQCadj should never be trusted without being checked.

Development status

Initial public release: v0.1.0

Citation

If you use miQCadj in published work, please cite the package as well as miQC, and flexmix packages.

Package citation information is available in R using:

citation("miQCadj")
citation("miQC")
citation("flexmix")

Alternatively, the citation for miQCadj, miQC, and flexmix can be copied below:

miQCadj

Spies E (2026). "miQCadj: Extensions and Utilities for miQC-based Cell Filtering." R package version 0.1.0.

miQC

Hippen A, Falco M, Weber L, Erkan E, Zhang K, Doherty J, Vähärautio A, Greene C, Hicks S (2021). “miQC: An adaptive probabilistic framework for quality control of single-cell RNA-sequencing data.” PLoS Comput Biol. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009290.

flexmix

Gruen B, Leisch F (2026). flexmix: Flexible Mixture Modeling. doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.flexmix. R package version 2.3-21, https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=flexmix.
